title: Retry-safe SDDC Manager network-pool reconciliation
prompt:
Complete the root Go package `networkpoolensure` (module `vcf91-0036`, standard library only) as a focused VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager REST integration. Creating a network pool is a POST, but callers must be able to retry an ensure operation after an uncertain transport outcome without creating the same pool twice. Collection output must also remain deterministic when SDDC Manager changes element order.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. It was derived from that OpenAPI specification, not a rendered documentation page. The exact specification path, repository commit SHA, and every operationId are repeated in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. The only operationIds in scope are `getNetworkPool` and `createNetworkPool`; do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

Preserve the public models and error types declared in `client.go` and implement these rules:

- `NewClient(Config)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin and performs no traffic. Reject embedded credentials, query (including a dangling `?`), fragment, a non-root path, and a blank or ASCII-whitespace-bearing access token. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Copy the selected HTTP client and disable redirect following without mutating the caller's client.
- `ListNetworkPools(ctx)` invokes exactly `GET /v1/network-pools`, with no query or body. Send `Accept: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; do not send `Content-Type` or a dangling query delimiter. Accept exactly HTTP 200 with an `application/json` media type. Require `elements` and `pageMetadata`, validate the one-page metadata against the actual element count, and require nonblank unique pool IDs and nonblank names. Preserve every decoded field. Return a copy sorted by `name`, then `id`, using Go's case-sensitive string ordering. Return a non-nil empty slice for an empty collection and never return service order.
- `EnsureNetworkPool(ctx, spec)` validates before traffic. `Name` must be nonblank with no surrounding whitespace and `Networks` must be a non-nil array. Each network requires a nonblank, trimmed `Type`; `VLANID` and `MTU` must fit signed int32. Presence-aware optional strings reject empty, surrounding-whitespace values; `IPAddressVersion`, when present, is `IPv4` or `IPv6`, and `IPAddressAssignmentMode` is `STATIC`, `DHCP`, or `SLAAC`. Every IP pool requires trimmed, nonblank `Start` and `End` values.
- Serialize `NetworkPoolSpec` once as compact UTF-8 JSON. Required request members are `name`, `networks`, and, within each network, `type`, `vlanId`, and `mtu`. Unset optional fields must be absent rather than null or empty. Never send read-only `id`, `hostsCount`, `freeIps`, `usedIps`, `usedIpCount`, or `freeIpCount` in the create body.
- Reconcile under a per-client, context-interruptible gate so concurrent ensures for the same client cannot race into duplicate POSTs. First call `getNetworkPool`. If no pool has the requested name, invoke exactly `POST /v1/network-pools` once, with no query, the same GET headers plus `Content-Type: application/json`, and the serialized body. Accept exactly HTTP 201 `application/json`; require a nonblank returned ID and require its writable configuration to equal the request. Return `Created: true`.
- If exactly one listed pool has the requested name and its writable configuration equals the request, return it with `Created: false` and send no POST. If its writable configuration differs, return `*DriftError`; if multiple listed pools have the name, return `*AmbiguousMatchError`. Neither case may mutate. This lookup-before-create rule is the retry guarantee: do not automatically retry POST. If a POST commits but its response is lost, that call returns a transport error; a later call must discover the committed pool through GET and must not POST again.
- Bound response bodies to 1 MiB, close every body, reject malformed, trailing, oversized, or wrong-media-type success data with `*ProtocolError`, and stop traffic after a failure. Decode non-success Error envelopes into `*APIError`, preserving operationId, status, errorCode, message, remediationMessage, and referenceToken. Use `*TransportError` for transport/read failures and preserve causes for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, including context cancellation. Error strings must not expose the bearer token, response body, decoded server/remediation message, reference token, or underlying transport exception text.

The protected `internal/contractmock` fixture loads and pins exactly those two routes from `docs/contract.json`, listens only on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates tokens, IDs, and names at runtime, and exposes a race-safe request log and mutation-effect count. It reverses the network-pool elements on every collection response. Protected table-driven tests verify provenance hashes, exact methods, targets, headers and compact body bytes, omission of read-only and unset fields, stable sorting, local validation, drift/ambiguity handling, concurrency, structured and protocol errors, redirect behavior, and retry after a committed-but-lost POST response. A client that returns collection service order fails deterministically. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Do not modify `go.mod`, `contract_test.go`, `.gitignore`, `docs/`, or `internal/contractmock/`; edit only `client.go`. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.
